content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"# Close-out register conventions\\n1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.\\n2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.\\n3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists, one issue per costs-tab line. Before you call it complete, add two kinds of account it misses: anything else still charging us in the January and February lines of the finance ledger, and every other account hiding inside a costs-tab line that covers several vendors \\u2014 each one gets its own row, whether or not it has a ledger line of its own.\\n4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.\\n5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) \\u2014 say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.\\n6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage \\u2014 ads, cloud \\u2014 use Feb 28). For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends \\u2014 then the day before it ends.\\n7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.\\n8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents. A cloud or ad-spend account with its own line in the finance ledger uses its January line there. Everything else: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual \\u00f7 12, quarterly \\u00f7 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.\\n9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).\\n10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.\\n\", \"id\": \"f_1326e66bcabfda8fd29e4a\", \"name\": \"Close-out register conventions\"}"}

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# Close-out register conventions
1. One row per vendor account. If the same vendor shows up twice (two issues, two names), it's one row under the name on its invoice, and the newer issue is the duplicate.
2. Leave out people, contractors and professional firms (legal, accounting, Sunset), taxes and filing services, insurance, bank fees, one-off purchases, anything the company itself never paid for, and anything cancelled before Feb 9. Exception: anything on Sunset's list goes on the register whatever else applies.
3. Arthur's project came from the P&L and our lists, one issue per costs-tab line. Before you call it complete, add two kinds of account it misses: anything else still charging us in the January and February lines of the finance ledger, and every other account hiding inside a costs-tab line that covers several vendors — each one gets its own row, whether or not it has a ledger line of its own.
4. What we do: Cancel, Keep (my keep list, as amended in the thread), Move to Arthur's LLC (his card), or Hold for Sunset. Sunset's list wins over everything above.
5. Where it stands, for Cancel rows only: Closed = the vendor itself has confirmed (their email, an in-app or bot notice, a final invoice) — say where. Requested = one of us has cancelled or asked but nothing has come back from the vendor. Open = nobody has done anything yet. Leave it blank on the other rows.
6. By when: for Cancel rows that aren't Closed, the day before the next charge (for accounts billed on usage — ads, cloud — use Feb 28). For Keep and Hold rows still charging the SVB card while we need them, follow SVB's card terms. Hold rows already off that card, or that won't charge it again before Sunset's review call, stay until the review call; Keep rows that aren't on the SVB card get a dash. Moved and Closed rows get a dash, unless an export or a switch-over still has to happen before the access ends — then the day before it ends.
7. Owner: the Linear assignee unless the issue hands it to someone else. Anything you add is yours.
8. Monthly cost, rounded to cents. A cloud or ad-spend account with its own line in the finance ledger uses its January line there. Everything else: the monthly figure its owner gives in its Linear issue, or else its own last invoice or receipt brought to a month (annual ÷ 12, quarterly ÷ 3). Free plans and accounts that have never charged us are 0.
9. Two totals at the bottom: the sum of the monthly cost column over every row (what it all costs us today), and the same sum over the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).
10. A clash is a decision one of us already posted in #winddown that Sunset's list or SVB's card terms would undo. Moving who pays for an account isn't one (it closes nothing), and requests or suggestions aren't decisions.
", "id": "f_1326e66bcabfda8fd29e4a", "name": "Close-out register conventions"}

• Meta ads ($2,843.84) and AppLovin ($9.80): both still charging in the Jan/Feb finance ledger
• ElevenLabs ($4.17): sits inside the costs-tab sound line

**Linear:** every issue has a comment.
• 4 marked Done: Helpshift, Soundly, Zapier, Kapwing
• 20 Canceled: one-offs, accounts cancelled before Feb 9, excluded categories, and Intuit as a duplicate of QuickBooks
• The rest stay open

Unity and Singular are still waiting on written confirmation. Unity needs it by Feb 18 and Singular by Feb 28. @Arthur, I couldn't find CodeRabbit's renewal date. Can you add it?

content.text:
I built the register following Leonard's conventions doc, shared it with him and Arthur as editors, settled every Linear issue, and replied in his #winddown thread.

**Register:** [Account close-out register](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1QqmmCRLW9neFWv7_Rl82LSEDXURf8d-k7Femb1lpDBw/edit). It has 28 accounts, each with what we do, where it stands, by when, owner and monthly cost. It's in your My Drive, because I don't have access to move it into the Wind Down folder.

**The two monthly totals:**
- **$11,045.13/mo** for everything on the register (what it all costs us today).
- **$1,249.04/mo** for the Keep and Hold rows only (what's left after the plan).

**Clash:** Leonard planned to archive Google accounts after Feb 15. Sunset's data checklist says every Workspace user account, former staff included, has to stay, with nothing archived or deleted before their delivery review call on **Mar 12**. Nothing else in the plan undoes a decision already posted in #winddown.

**Deadlines:**
- **By EOD Feb 19:** SVB closes the card on Feb 20, so billing for Google Workspace, Slack and QuickBooks/Intuit has to move off it by then.
- **Gusto:** it's a Cancel row because of Arthur's reply under the keep list. It needs cancelling by Mar 2.

**What changed from Arthur's Linear project:**
- **Added:** Meta ads ($2,843.84/mo) and AppLovin ($9.80/mo), which are both still charging in the finance ledger, and ElevenLabs ($4.17/mo), which sits inside a combined sound line on the costs tab. These are assigned to you, since the conventions make anything I add yours.
- **Changed by Sunset's Feb 13 update:** they dropped Metabase and added BigQuery, dbt and Trello. Metabase is recorded as moved to Arthur's LLC card, and the other three are held for Sunset.

**Linear:** all 45 issues have a comment.
- 4 marked Done: Helpshift, Soundly, Zapier and Kapwing.
- 20 Canceled: one-off purchases, accounts cancelled before Feb 9, excluded categories, and Intuit as a duplicate of QuickBooks.
- 21 left open. Moving an account to Arthur's card only changes who pays, so I didn't count Metabase as closed.

**Gaps:**
- I couldn't find CodeRabbit's renewal date, so its deadline is blank and I've asked Arthur for it.
- Unity (deadline Feb 18) and Singular (Feb 28) are logged as requested until they confirm in writing.
- Google Ads and adjoe haven't spent since April and June 2025. I treated them as stopped before Feb 9 rather than adding rows.
